audit.why: 55.78% over 147 games. The page gives Cassiopeia levels 1 through first item and K'Sante the 2+ item window, which matches the shape of poison-mage versus scaling tank.

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out was the page's whole clock and never carried a number, and the page never said the spike cuts both ways.
audit.why: All Out is 120s at rank 1 — the same as Petrifying Gaze — and Riot's own text says he gains damage, healing and transformed abilities 'at the cost of reduced defenses'. The moment he goes All Out is the moment a poison mage's damage is worth most, which reframes his spike as a shared window rather than purely his.
audit.corrected: 120s and the resist cost written into full.breakdown.cooldowns and full.loading; Footwork 10s and Path Maker 14s added alongside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six places built the lane plan around 'his Q knockup' (spikes[1].text, early, mid, wants.foe[0], whys[0], whys[2]). Ntofo Strikes does not knock up.
audit.why: Riot: Ntofo Strikes 'strikes, damaging and slowing enemies in a short line. On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' It is a slow and then a pull — the knockups in his kit are Path Maker and All Out. The difference matters to a champion with no dash: a pull drags you toward him, so the tell to react to is the second Q stack landing, not an airborne animation that never happens. The page also never named Footwork, the dash Miasma most cleanly answers, or the shield that comes with it.
audit.corrected: The pull replaces the knockup in all six places, Footwork and Path Maker are named as the two grounded dashes, and the Footwork shield now appears in full.report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early said his W 'can block one poke'.
audit.why: Path Maker is not a block. Riot: 'K'Sante charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes.' Damage reduction while charging means a poke thrown into it is discounted rather than deleted — and it means burst spent into the charge is the worst-timed damage in the matchup.
audit.corrected: content.early now states the damage reduction directly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization never mentioned anti-heal, and nothing warned that stacking resistances is the wrong answer here.
audit.why: All Out grants healing, and Path Maker deals true damage — so raw armour or MR does nothing about his committed damage while Grievous Wounds does something about his committed sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said All Out can put a wall between you and safety.
audit.why: Riot: All Out 'knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path.' Cassiopeia owns no dash, so being launched over terrain is unrecoverable without Flash — which makes the summoner a terrain answer in this matchup, not a damage answer.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze (R) answers his All Out all-in — when he W-dashes or lands his Q knockup to commit, FACE him so the cone stuns instead of slows, then E-spam him while he's locked and his resists are stripped by his own R.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze (R) answers his All Out all-in — when he Path Makers in or drags you with a second Ntofo Strikes stack, FACE him so the cone stuns instead of slows, then E-spam while he's locked and All Out has stripped his resists.

edits.before: Level 1 he is a durable point-and-click trader — his W can block one poke and his Q knockup sets up a step-in, so don't throw a lone Noxious Blast he eats for free and punishes. This is a discipline check: just farm and build the poison economy until Level 3. Once you hit 3, prime him with Q and chain Twin Fang on the refund — your E out-damages anything his tank form can trade back. The thing to respect is his Q-knockup into a walk-up; bait that cooldown, then poke.
edits.after: Level 1 he is a durable point-and-click trader — Path Maker reduces the damage he takes while he charges it, and two Ntofo Strikes stacks pull you in for a step-up, so don't throw a lone Noxious Blast he eats for free. This is a discipline check: farm and build the poison economy until Level 3. Once you hit 3, prime him with Q and chain Twin Fang on the refund — your E out-damages anything his tank form can trade back. Bait the pull, then poke.

edits.before: This is your lane. Hold W Miasma for the exact moment he tries to W-dash or step in off his Q knockup — the grounding cloud disables the dash and lets your Serpentine Grace move speed kite him forever. At 6, stop fearing All Out: when he commits, FACE him so Petrifying Gaze stuns rather than slows, then E-spam him while he's locked and his own R has stripped his resists. Take plates behind that poison threat and fight at river where your sustained DPS goes unanswered.
edits.after: This is your lane. Hold W Miasma for the exact moment he Footwork-dashes or Path Makers in — the grounding cloud kills both dashes and lets your Serpentine Grace move speed kite him forever. At 6, stop fearing All Out: when he commits, FACE him so Petrifying Gaze stuns rather than slows, then E-spam him while he's locked and his own R has stripped his resists. Take plates behind that poison threat and fight at river where your DPS goes unanswered.

edits.after: Stack two Ntofo Strikes to pull you in, then walk up for a real trade before your W can ground him

edits.after: Save W Miasma for his Footwork or Path Maker dash — the grounding zone disables both, so the tank physically cannot close on you

edits.after: Discipline check at 1 — a lone Q feeds a Path Maker that reduces his damage taken, and two Ntofo Strikes stacks pull a careless step-up, so farm the poison economy instead.

edits.after: W Miasma grounds both Footwork and Path Maker — the tank loses every single tool that closes the gap on you.

edits.before: Track K'Sante’s All Out: His duelist mode — fight the tank, never the duelist. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Footwork and Path Maker. Force the Footwork shield out before you commit — burst spent into it is wasted.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode — fight the tank, never the duelist. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Miasma like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - All Out: 120s at rank 1, and it strips his own resists — that window is yours too. - Footwork is 10s and shields; force it out early. - Path Maker is 14s and reduces his damage taken while he charges.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia vs K'Sante - Track: K'Sante All Out. - E only poisoned targets — mana is the lane. - All Out down is the green light. - Hold the ult for names, not waves.
edits.after: - Cassiopeia vs K'Sante - Track: All Out, 120s. - E only poisoned targets — mana is the lane. - W grounds Footwork and Path Maker. - Hold Flash for his R wall.

edits.before: No boots — ever; her passive replaces them. Tear early, then Seraph's or Liandry's, Rylai's, and Rabadon's by game state.
edits.after: No boots — ever; her passive replaces them. Tear, then Liandry's, and anti-heal before All Out's healing carries the dive.

notes: Same internal contradiction as the Jax page: full.phases[6] and content.win[6] both hand '2+ items' to Cassiopeia, while content.spikes[3] and content.late both say a fed K'Sante reclaims it. I did not flip either — see questionsForUser. Note also that this matchup had no packet defects and no suspect names flagged, yet 'Q knockup' was wrong in six places; the defect scanner catches misspelled ability names, not correctly-spelled abilities credited with the wrong mechanic.
